document.abstract: The scrambling technique used in the SMPTE serial digital interface (SDI) standards can produce so-called pathological conditions—long runs of 1s or 0s that challenge the capabilities of the receiving equipment and may lead to bit errors if not handled correctly. This paper revisits how pathological conditions can arise and makes some new observations with respect to pathological conditions in 1.5 Gbit/s and recently-standardized 3 Gbit/s HD SDI links.

authors.bio: David Brown is strategic technology manager for 40/100G ICs for optical modules and line cards within the Mixed Signal and Optical (MSO) Products Group of Gennum Corp. With a seasoned background in custom IC design, product definition and marketing, he joined Gennum's Analog and Mixed Signal division (now MSO) in 2006. Brown graduated with degrees in engineering physics and electrical engineering from Queen's University at Kingston in 1983 and 1985.
authors.name: David Brown

authors.bio: John Hudson is director of broadcast technology at Gennum Corp. in Burlington Canada. He began his career in the broadcast industry in 1984 when he joined the Design and Development group of Sony Broadcast and Professional Europe as a technician engineer. During his career, he has worked as a design engineer, project leader, system architect, program manager, product definition engineer, and technology strategist. — Hudson is active in television standards work. He is Co-Chair of TC10E and chairs the 32NF20 Electrical Interfaces Working Group in SMPTE. He also chairs the Technical Committee of the HDcctv Alliance, which is responsible for the development of standards for the HDcctv Industry.
